title: Hunt the boundaries
prompt: `countUniqueWords` passes every happy-path test. Write `main` printing one PASS/FAIL line per edge case you believe it must survive: empty string, only whitespace, single word, duplicated words ("the the"), mixed case ("The THE"), and words with punctuation adjacent ("hello,world"). Run it - at least one case should surprise you - then harden `countUniqueWords` so every one of your cases prints PASS (treat "hello,world" as two words by splitting on any non-letter).

tests.name: core counting still works
tests.code:
CjTestBase.checkEq(Solution.countUniqueWords("the quick brown fox"), 4, "four unique words");
CjTestBase.checkEq(Solution.countUniqueWords("the the THE"), 1, "case-insensitive duplicates");
tests.hint: Keep the lowercase normalization - the hardening is about splitting, not case.

tests.name: punctuation no longer glues words
tests.hint: split("[^a-z]+") after lowercasing splits on every non-letter run.

tests.name: empty and blank survive
tests.hint: Guard first; then the split never sees a blank string.
